_about: Electricity tariffs the operator pays at the depot. Every figure was read from the regulator's order named in `source`; none is a guess. Vendor or news figures are not used.

msedcl_ht_ix.label: Pune, MSEDCL HT IX (HT EV charging station)
msedcl_ht_ix.unit: Rs per kVAh, treated as Rs per kWh
msedcl_ht_ix.source: MERC Order in Case No. 75 of 2025 (post-remand), 25 March 2026, Annexure II, 'Summary of HT Tariff for FY 2026-27' (page 100 of 123): HT IX energy charge 8.92, wheeling charge 0.81 (EHV supply has no wheeling charge)

msedcl_lt_viii.label: Pune, MSEDCL LT VIII (LT EV charging station)
msedcl_lt_viii.unit: Rs per kVAh, treated as Rs per kWh
msedcl_lt_viii.source: MERC Order in Case No. 75 of 2025 (post-remand), 25 March 2026, Annexure II, 'Summary of LT Tariff for FY 2026-27' (page 95 of 123): LT VIII energy charge 7.73, wheeling charge 1.52, no fixed charge

time_of_day.notes: Case 75 of 2025, paras 18.13 and 18.14 and Table 8: the night rebate (00:00 to 06:00) is removed, so 00:00 to 09:00 is 0 %. Solar hours 09:00 to 17:00 are a rebate of 15 % in April to September and 25 % in October to March for FY 2026-27, which averages 20 % over the year. Peak hours 17:00 to 24:00 carry +20 % in Table 8. The order's footnote for the peak rate was not in the text extracted; the MERC press note on Case 217 of 2024 (Note 3 to its ToD table) applies +20 % at peak to every category other than residential, group housing and agriculture, which includes EV charging. Check the first bill.

not_included: power-factor penalty (the tariff is per kVAh and is treated here as per kWh at unity power factor)
